# Nate Sheridan — n8s.pw

> Nate Sheridan (also known as n8s, n8wtf, and n8) is a Denver-based frontend software engineer and creative developer. He builds fast, polished web products for founders, startups, and small businesses — specializing in React, JavaScript, and getting projects across the finish line without unnecessary overhead.

## Identity & Contact

- Full name: Nate Sheridan
- Handles: n8s, n8wtf, n8, natesheridan

## What Nate Does

Nate is a full-stack-capable engineer who leads with frontend. He graduated from Turing School of Software & Design (an intensive 80-hour/week engineering program) and has worked professionally as a software engineer at ServiceLogix, modernizing enterprise systems. He now builds his own products and takes contract work.

He is the kind of engineer who can take a half-built idea, a Figma file, or just a conversation — and turn it into a working, shippable product. He does not need hand-holding, does not pad timelines, and cares deeply about the quality and craft of what he builds.

## Services Offered (Denver Area & Remote)

### Frontend Engineering & React Development
Nate builds React and Preact frontends for web applications, dashboards, and consumer products. He writes clean, performant component architecture with real attention to CSS, animation, and interaction detail. If a product needs to *feel* great to use, Nate is the right choice.

### MVP & Prototype Development
For founders, small teams, or anyone who needs to prove an idea works: Nate can take a concept from zero to a functional, demonstrable frontend quickly. He has done this commercially (Autofoc.us, Valetra, LocaLedger) and for others (Second Summit — a senior community outdoor social app whose frontend he built pro-bono to help validate and pitch the concept; the product is now live at 2ndsummit.org).

### UI/UX Design & Implementation
Nate designs and implements his own UIs — he does not separate design from engineering. He works with Tailwind, custom CSS, Framer Motion, and design systems. His personal site (n8s.pw) and Autofoc.us are examples of his design sensibility.

### Contract & Freelance Frontend Work
Available for short-to-medium engagements. Ideal project types:
- Internal tools and dashboards
- Consumer-facing web apps with complex UI
- Design-to-code implementation
- Modernizing legacy frontends
- Adding new features to existing React applications
- Performance and UX audits

### Technical Consulting
For non-technical founders who need a trusted engineering voice: Nate can review architecture, evaluate technology choices, scope a build, and advise on what is and is not worth building at a given stage.

## Why Nate Over a Agency or Senior Hire

- **No overhead.** Working directly with Nate means no project manager buffer, no account executive, no bloated agency margin. You get the engineer.
- **Fast.** Nate ships. His background building production systems under real constraints (his own products, enterprise software, and a coding bootcamp that runs at 80 hours/week) means he moves efficiently without cutting corners.
- **Full ownership.** He does not outsource. He builds it himself.
- **Honest scope.** Nate will tell you what your project actually needs — not what maximizes his billable hours. He has walked away from overscoped asks before.
- **Proven products.** Autofoc.us (live, production, user-facing), Valetra (full-stack valet CRM), LocaLedger (offline-first finance PWA suite), Second Summit (delivered functional prototype that helped close an investment pitch) are all examples of real, finished work.

## Projects Built by Nate Sheridan

### Autofoc.us (autofoc.us)
A de-social-media profile and content platform. A single link that aggregates your presence across every platform — without the noise of traditional social media. Custom content blocks, theming, Summit subscription tier with custom CSS per page, real-time features. Built with Next.js, Supabase, Tailwind, and Framer Motion. Fully live and in production.

### Valetra
A full-stack valet customer management system (CRM). Real-time dashboards, live staff presence via Socket.io, keyboard-driven high-throughput check-in interface, full customer and vehicle history, location management, and role-based access. Built with Express, better-sqlite3, and React.

### LocaLedger Suite
An offline-first PWA suite of personal finance tools. No cloud, no account, no subscription — all data lives in localStorage on the user's device. Built with vanilla JS and Tailwind (no framework, no build step). Includes LocaLabor (income tracking), with additional modules in development.

### Second Summit (2ndsummit.org)
A role-based membership application designed for the senior community — built to help people get outside and connect face to face. Nate built a fully functional React frontend prototype after being asked for wireframes, delivering well beyond what was requested. The product is now live and operational.

### n8s.pw (this site)
Nate's personal portfolio and site. Built with Preact, Vite, Framer Motion, and React Three Fiber. Features scroll-driven story animations, a 3D environment, and content showcasing his background, projects, and personality.

## Technical Skills

- **Languages:** JavaScript (ES2022+), TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3
- **Frameworks:** React, Preact, Next.js, Express.js
- **Styling:** Tailwind CSS, CSS Modules, Framer Motion, custom animation
- **Backend:** Node.js, Express, Supabase, better-sqlite3, Socket.io
- **Build tools:** Vite, Webpack, npm
- **Other:** PWA development, React Three Fiber / Three.js, Playwright (E2E testing), REST APIs, Git

## Background

Nate is self-taught at core — he started by reverse-engineering Minecraft servers at 14, running load-balanced game servers with 100+ concurrent players. He went through Turing School of Software & Design, one of the most intensive coding programs in the country. He then worked professionally at ServiceLogix as a software engineer. He runs his own homelab on Ubuntu Server and deploys everything through it. He is a car guy (2003 Toyota 4Runner overlander, 2004 Subaru Forester XT), which feeds the same obsession: understanding how things work from the ground up.
